hlni.insight: A degree title is not an assessment method; task-level evaluation criteria define the actual learning experience.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume that degree names like B.Com or BBA inherently define the type of work or feedback they will receive.
hlni.viewerChange: Learns to isolate assessment criteria from titles, enabling precise questions during course selection.
hlni.support: The three-column audit method forces the student to look for objective assessment standards rather than relying on program branding.
hlni.payoff: The method turns abstract comparisons into a concrete inquiry about rubrics and feedback, which is the actual differentiator for a student's day-to-day academic experience.

shots.name: Initial Confusion
shots.visual: A student looking at a course booklet, looking torn between B.Com and BBA labels.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA based on titles alone is a trap. The degree name doesn't tell you how you will actually be graded.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close up on the student, shifting focus to the booklet.

shots.name: The Audit Method
shots.visual: Student holds a three-column worksheet. They fill in a row for a sample task.
shots.dialogue: Try this audit. Write the task, then identify the assessment criteria and feedback. If you can't fill those in, you have your question.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Calculate break-even. Graded on: ? Feedback: ?
shots.cameraPerformance: Handheld shot focusing on the pen writing on the paper.

shots.name: The Concrete Question
shots.visual: Student points to the question marks on the sheet, looking empowered.
shots.dialogue: Now ask: What specific rubric is used to evaluate this calculation? That's how you compare.
shots.onscreenText: What specific rubric is used to evaluate this calculation?
shots.cameraPerformance: Medium shot, student looks directly at the camera.

productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic cuts matching the audit steps
